name: vbindiff
why: Side-by-side visual binary diff that makes byte-level changes between files pop out in a way few people have tried.

brief.what_it_is: VBinDiff (Visual Binary Diff) is a terminal and Windows program that displays files in hexadecimal and ASCII (or EBCDIC). It can show two files at once and highlight the bytes that differ between them. It can also browse a single file in hex mode. Input is one or two file paths; output is an interactive full-screen hex view on screen. The homepage describes it as working well with large files, up to 4 GB, unlike diff.
brief.why_it_exists: The author, Christopher J. Madsen, was inspired by the Compare Files function of the ProSel utilities for the Apple II. When he could not find a similar utility for the PC, he wrote one. The single-file mode was modeled on the LIST utility of 4DOS, because less has no equivalent hex display.
brief.how_it_works: The README gives no internals beyond the interface description. It shows the two files in a side-by-side hex and ASCII view and highlights differing bytes. The author notes that piping a file through hexdump is very inefficient on multi-gigabyte files, which is the reason for building the viewer as its own tool.

commands_seen.context: Developer setup from the GitHub README: pulls in the Free GetOpt submodule after cloning the repository.
Developer setup on Unix, run after the submodule step and before the normal configure and make process.
Standard Unix build of VBinDiff from source once autoreconf has run.
Optional for Unix developers: installs a git hook that regenerates configure after commits that modify configure.ac.

brief.install_notes: Downloads on the homepage: VBinDiff 3.0 beta 5 as source only for Linux and POSIX systems, and as an exe plus source for Windows 9x through 10. Building from a git clone needs git submodule update --init, then autoreconf -i on Unix, then ./configure && make. On Windows, the project file is win32/vbindiff.dsw, built with Visual Studio 2015. Building the documentation also needs Perl, Date::Format and Template-Toolkit; Strawberry Perl is recommended on Windows, and distro package names are listed for Arch, Gentoo and Ubuntu. No accounts or runtime services are required.
brief.standout: It is a single-purpose binary comparison viewer that handles very large files, which the author says the standard diff tools do not. Its lineage runs from an Apple II utility through OS/2 and then Win32, and it is still a small C program that ships as source for POSIX systems.
brief.status: Quiet. The latest release, 3.0 beta 5, is dated 10 September 2017, and the homepage was last modified on the same date. The release history stops at 2017. The fetched README does not show a last commit date, and the README says development moved to Git on GitHub. The project is in beta and has not had a stable 3.0 release in the pages I read.
brief.caveats: Still labelled beta (3.0 beta 5). The Windows build needs Visual Studio 2015, and the docs need a Perl toolchain. Single files are limited to 4 GB according to the homepage. The Unix build needs autoreconf because the repository uses a submodule. The homepage asks for feedback from users and does not describe a roadmap. Licensed under GPL v2 or later. The homepage itself is not affected by any caveat from brew, since the brew caveats field is empty.
quotes: VBinDiff (Visual Binary Diff) displays files in hexadecimal and ASCII (or EBCDIC).
Unlike diff, it works well with large files (up to 4 GB).
(True, you can pipe the file through hexdump, but that's incredibly inefficient on multi-gigabyte files.)
